cc8eb1b63fd50236: CONSPIRACY THEORISTS

FOR months, conspiracy-peddling supporters of President Donald Trump spread baseless theories that the vote would be rigged. But those claims all but dried up after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.

Political pundits had anticipated a wave of legal challenges from election deniers seeking to contest the results of Tuesday's vote, or efforts by Trump himself to tilt the outcome in his favour — as he did when he tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat.
But none of that materialised.
And evidence-free claims of fraud slowed to a trickle after what observers called the decisive "blue tsunami" of Democratic victories that handed the party control of both chambers of Congress.
Trump's acceptance of the results, signalling he would not challenge his Republican Party's sweeping defeat, set the tone for many of his loyalists to follow suit.
"Election day 2026 featured a few rumours about election integrity.

"However, election denialism was not a core narrative used to explain the sweeping victories by Democrats once they became apparent," said the University of Washington's Center for an Informed Public.
"Absent a political elite to champion election denialism, rumouring about election integrity has not coalesced into a coherent or significant narrative to explain election results."
Many analysts said the scale of the Democratic victory — widely seen as a repudiation of Trump's political agenda — may have played a role.

However, David Becker, executive director of the nonpartisan Center for Election Innovation and Research, argued that fraud claims persisted in the past even when the president's preferred candidates lost by large margins.
"I don't know necessarily that margin of victory makes much difference to those who have profited off the economy of grift around election conspiracies for quite some time," Becker said.
"It might be that politics overall in the nation have changed to some degree, and that creates a different incentive structure."
It also did not help that many election deniers on the ballot lost their races — and chose not to challenge the results.
Among them was Andy Biggs, one of the Republican politicians who joined Trump in challenging the 2020 election results after his defeat to Joe Biden.
After losing Arizona's gubernatorial race, Biggs conceded to incumbent Democrat Katie Hobbs, making no mention of voter fraud and instead blaming what he perceived as a low voter turnout.
"We just didn't get our turnout quite as full as we wanted to," he said in comments reported by US media.
Even conservative influencers — including prominent supporters of Trump's Make America Great Again movement who have been vocal election sceptics — appeared subdued.

Ahead of the midterm elections, some sceptics went so far as to call for a "national emergency", urging Trump to grant himself "king-like powers" over the midterms, according to the left-leaning watchdog Media Matters for America.

"I have been banging the drum of rigged and stolen elections since 2020, but that is not why we lost the midterms," conservative political commentator Rogan O'Handley wrote to his 2.3 million followers on X.
"We lost because we failed to fix the things voters sent us to do... Lower gas and food prices and stop the Iran war."
Media Matters' John Knefel cautioned against "premature" hopes that "the election denial fever has permanently broken".
"Rejecting Democratic Party wins remains a core, foundational element of the movement that Trump built and will likely continue to be one for the foreseeable future," he said.
But striking a note of optimism, Becker said "American voters are tired" of evidence-free election denialism.

"A smaller number of election sceptics ran this time than in past cycles, and there seem to be substantially less stomach for these claims among voters," said Pamela Smith, president of the nonpartisan nonprofit Verified Voting.
Citing an independent poll, Smith added: "Most voters are interested in other issues — fraud in elections does not seem to be a driver for deciding their vote."
* The writer is from AFP

5431307acddb99ff: ISTANBUL: Malaysia and Turkiye's trade target of US$10 billion by 2030 is achievable, especially through the procurement of defence and security equipment.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the balance of trade between both countries is currently in Malaysia's favour.
"From the effort of both countries, the target is achievable, especially from Malaysia, in procuring defence and security equipment," he said.
Zahid was speaking at a panel session titled "Turkiye: From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor" at the 2026 TRT World Forum here today.

Other panellists included Foundation for Political, Economic and Social Research (SETA) Foreign Policy Studies director Prof Murat Yesiltas; Atlantic Council non-resident senior fellow Dr Rich Outzen; American Arab Center president Farah Al-Atassi; and United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations Jean-Pierre Lacroix.

The forum, themed "A World Without a Center: Who Leads When the Rules Run Out?", brings together political leaders, policymakers, academics, media practitioners and civil society representatives to discuss global issues.
The forum was launched by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
He said Malaysia has taken delivery of Littoral Mission Ships and unmanned aerial vehicles from Turkiye. This, he said, would strengthen ties not only in defence and security, but also in trade.
"I think extra effort will be taken by both countries to achieve the target," he said.
Meanwhile, Zahid said Malaysia views defence cooperation with Turkiye as a strategic choice and not just a procurement exercise, as it involves the transfer of knowledge and technology.
"Turkiye occupies a strategic position connecting Europe, West Asia, Central Asia and surrounding regions. That is why I think close collaboration between Malaysia and Turkiye is important," he said.

Zahid said Malaysia also viewed Turkiye's status as a 12th Asean Dialogue Partner as an opportunity for more structured cooperation that delivers tangible benefits, rather than adding another diplomatic platform.
He said military diplomacy was also important to keep Southeast Asia peaceful and politically stable, and to prevent major powers from influencing Asean member states.
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, is in Turkiye for a four-day working visit from Nov 5 to 8.
Malaysia and Turkiye established diplomatic relations on June 17, 1964, and have since maintained close ties in politics, the economy, trade and education.
Malaysia is one of Turkiye's largest trading partners in Southeast Asia.
Bilateral trade stands at US$5.6 billion, and both countries aim to raise it to US$10 billion by 2030 following an agreement between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Erdogan in January.

6f58dd6a990a6165: <!--kg-card-end: html--> Immediately after the UK banned a wide range of porn fantasies involving choking, breath-restriction, and relative roleplay, adult creators watched platforms remove hundreds of their videos — even when the creators thought they were in compliance with the law. These creators say they were blindsided by the removals, since the content didn’t seem to violate the law at all.
Creators are reporting one platform in particular, Clips4Sale, is purging content with little notice, “a precautionary measure.”

Some creators who’ve contacted Clips4Sale to appeal these removals have shared screenshots online of the reply the platform sends: “At this time, we have implemented a general restriction on content availability in the UK to ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements,” Clips4Sale support replies, according to these screenshots, viewed by 404 Media. “This is a precautionary measure and does not necessarily indicate that your clips contain prohibited content or violate our policies. We are continuing to review affected content, and additional clips will be made available to UK buyers as they are reviewed and cleared.”
In the UK, Face Sitting Porn Might Land You in Jail
The Crime and Policing Act, which goes into force on November 6, criminalizes possessing or publishing strangulation or suffocation porn, as well as some types of "close familial relatives" roleplay.

Updates to the UK’s Crime and Policing Act went into force on Friday. The law criminalizes a list of sexual acts, including downloading or publishing choking and incest roleplay content. The law is vague and overbroad, criminalizing “strangulation or suffocation” and “certain types” of incest roleplay. There's a lot of confusion among sex workers and fans about what this encompasses, and seemingly could include various kinds of gagging, face sitting, and roleplay. Violating this law, either as someone in possession of noncompliant content or publishing it, carries a risk of up to five years in prison.

UK-based creator Sophia Truee told me that Clips4Sale removed more than 75 percent of her content — 392 out of 506 videos — with the platform flagging it as requiring edits without noting what needed to change. Truee makes POV content where she’s alone talking to the camera. Many more creators have shared on social media that content that shouldn’t be in violation of the law has been caught in the crossfire on Clips4Sale specifically.

In an email sent to creators on Thursday, the day before the law went into force, Clips4Sale said it would be reviewing “both the video content and its details, including titles, tags, keywords, and descriptions” of content that creators have uploaded to the site. It told creators no action was required. “Affected clips will be hidden automatically starting November 6. If you'd like to make a clip available in the UK again, you can edit the content or its details as needed and submit the changes for compliance review.” Approved content would go back up, the company said.

Another message from Clips4Sale on creators’ dashboards said: “As we gain further clarity on the regulatory requirements, we expect to be able to make additional content available again to UK users, wherever permitted. These restrictions apply only to the UK and will not affect your content's availability in other markets where it is permitted.” According to the law, however, if creators based in the UK possess that content, they’re still facing jail time.

“Of course, we were all aware of the new Act coming in and prepared accordingly, but not for anything at this scale. We've had nothing since and they've been tweeting as normal,” Truee said. Clips4Sale launched in 2003 and caters heavily to fetish content. “It's a huge blow to this area of the industry, and I can only hope things will be communicated soon. We, as creators, understand how difficult it is to be a content site in this current climate, but communication has not been prioritized,” Truee said, noting that this is happening right before the holidays, with Black Friday being one of the most popular times for creators selling content. “For many, this will be devastating, as over 20 years of the work will have just been wiped.”

Are you affected by this new UK porn law, as a fan or creator? I would love to hear from you. Using a non-work device, you can message me securely on Signal at sam.404. Otherwise, send me an email at sam@404media.co.

Madame Caramel, another UK-based creator using Clips4Sale, posted on X that out of 900 clips she had available on the platform, she now has 198 left. Another creator, Goddess Kitty, wrote that the platform restricted 931 of her clips from UK audiences. “All of them [had] utterly NOTHING to do with the UK laws,” she wrote. There are many, many more creators across social media reporting that they’ve woken up to their clip sites gutted with no warning, even though their content wasn’t non-compliant by the letter of the law.

With the speed at which content has been purged en masse, and with some creators reporting instant rejections of content that should actually be compliant with the law, Clips4Sale may be auto-moderating with a very wide net, and sifting through reviews creators are now forced to send for legal content. This is something most social media platforms do to try to comply whenever over-broad laws or payment processor regulations hit.
Clips4Sale did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Other platforms are also attempting to comply now that the law is in effect. LoyalFans has a notice on its homepage for fans addressing the new law. It says: “These changes may also apply to content you've purchased, downloaded, or saved privately on your devices. Non-compliant content in your Loyalfans account will be removed on November 5, with no further action required from your side. We encourage you to understand the new law and review any affected content you have downloaded, or stored privately, whether on your phone, computer, or cloud storage.”

LoyalFans updated its terms of use on Thursday to include strangulation or suffocation, in its unacceptable content list, “including any content, whether real or simulated, that explicitly and realistically depicts a person strangling or suffocating another person, such as applying pressure to the neck or obstructing the nose or mouth,” the terms now say. “This content is prohibited regardless of whether the participants consent, and even if it is fantasy-based, roleplay, or digitally created.” Several creators using LoyalFans have posted on social media saying they’ve had hundreds of videos removed from their accounts on that platform, too.

JustForFans, an LGBTQ and kink content site, posted on X earlier this week that creators should review their content and use its new “restrict this content” option to keep it from being viewed by users in the UK. The platform also said that it would be scanning every new video upload for consent requirements and content restrictions. “If we find content that should be restricted in the UK, we will restrict it and you can review it in a new section of your Media Center called Restricted Content. The page will tell you what we found and give you options right on that page to fix it: re-word a post, replace a video with another video, delete the video, or tell us we are wrong, and why you believe we are wrong. A staff member will review your changes,” it said.

The vagueness of the law, combined with the use of auto-moderation on sites like Clips4Sale, have come together to create a nightmare for creators. “This highlights the lack of protection sex workers and content creators have when laws aren't properly researched and clearly written. We do our very best to stay compliant and ensure everyone's safety by following the rules,” Truee said. “This highlights the unprecedented use of AI in moderation and the lack of clear instructions from the government.”
a1d8ed0a9a894183: IN January last year, two former Sea Tackle Sdn Bhd directors, namely Teo Tzi Sin and Wong Poh Wah, were each fined RM100,000 for the offence of abusing their positions by using RM200,000 in company funds to pay themselves unauthorised bonuses.
They were charged under Section 218(1)(c) of the Companies Act 2016, read with Section 34 of the Penal Code.
The case clearly sends a clear message that company directors must carry out their functions and use their given authority in the company's interests, and not for personal benefit.

Under Section 218 of Companies Act 2016, directors and company officers who misuse their positions to benefit themselves or others, or to harm the company, may face up to five years in prison, a fine of up to RM3 million, or both.
But abuse of power does not happen only when directors take company money.

It can also involve directors awarding contracts to friends, family members or business associates, hiding personal interests, manipulating financial records, submitting false invoices and using confidential company information for personal gain.
The problem does not lie only with large corporations.

According to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission, corruption involving private-sector entities in 2025 amounted to approximately RM520 million, comprising RM124 million from listed companies, RM383 million from non-listed companies and RM11 million from sole proprietorships.
Under Section 213 of the Companies Act 2016, directors must act honestly, make decisions for proper reasons and put the company's interests first.

They must also use reasonable care, skill and attention when carrying out their duties. A director who breaks these legal duties may face up to five years in prison, a fine of up to RM3 million, or both.
Section 218 deals more directly with the misuse of a director's or company officer's position, company property, information or business opportunities for personal benefit or to harm the company.
The MACC Act 2009 also applies when corrupt payments are involved. Sections 16 and 17 deal with offering, giving, soliciting or receiving bribes by any person or by an agent.

Section 17A allows a company to be held liable when an associated person commits bribery to benefit the company. Section 23, meanwhile, deals with public officers who misuse their positions to obtain gratification.
It may also apply to officers of certain GLCs that qualify as public bodies under the act.
The Penal Code covers other offences, including criminal breach of trust, cheating, forgery, using false documents and falsifying company accounts.
The Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 covers market manipulation, false statements and insider trading, punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment and a minimum RM1 million fine.

One incident may involve several offences, but authorities must prove each offence; suspicious transactions alone does not mean someone is guilty. There is an important difference between making a poor business decision and deliberately breaking the law or committing error and fraud.

A director may make a business decision that turns out badly, which does not automatically mean that the director has committed a crime. However, directors must still take reasonable care and assess the risks before making decisions.

The situation is different when someone deliberately cheats the company, misappropriates money for personal use, accepts bribes or hides dishonest transactions where such actions may amount to criminal offences.
Laws in the country do not provide for "carelessness and stupidity" to be charged as offences.

In Hong Kong, public officers can face up to seven years in prison and a fine for seriously abusing their positions or deliberately neglecting their duties without a valid excuse, in breach of public trust.

Malaysia should continue to examine whether its laws provide sufficient protection when serious failures of responsibility lead to the misuse or loss of public money. Any criminal charge, however, must be supported by evidence and a clearly established legal offence.
Laws alone cannot prevent corporate abuse. Companies need a strong leadership, a clear tone at the top, effective controls and people committed to acting with honesty and integrity.
The Attorney-General's Chambers carries out the prosecution of criminal cases.
Ultimately, company directors and senior executives are entrusted with money, assets and the confidence of shareholders, employees and the public.
They must never forget that their positions carry a huge responsibility, not personal privileges.
* The writer is president of Malaysian Integrity and Governance Society (MIG) and professor of criminology at HELP University

aaf8c6a6e789dcd5: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is open to approving foreign workers for oil palm harvesting, provided the plantation industry commits to reducing its reliance on migrant labour through mechanisation.
He also said any abuse of workers, including foreign workers, must be met with firm action.

Speaking at the 14th Malaysia Madani Scholars Forum today, Anwar was responding to a question from a plantation industry representative who said most planters had yet to receive their foreign worker quotas for this year.

Also on the panel were Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, SD Guthrie Bhd president and group chief executive officer Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad, and PNB Research Institute chief executive officer Dr Sarena Che Omar.
The representative said machines were already being used for fertilising and weeding, but none were yet available for harvesting oil palm fruit, a task that still relied on foreign labour.
He told Anwar that recruitment took about three months, with a further three months needed for training.
Production could be affected next year if workers were not secured now, particularly with El Niño and haze expected, he said.
Anwar said he would view the matter "sympathetically" and raise it with the minister concerned.
He said the government could approve foreign workers for harvesting, on condition that the industry committed to reducing its reliance on them through mechanisation.
He said major plantation companies had not invested sufficiently in mechanisation to reduce their workforce, even when profits were high.
"A company makes a billion in profit. Raise wages by RM20 a month, they attack it. Until we, the government, had to make it mandatory.
"That is why I say the economy must also be humane," he said.
Anwar said Malaysia could not allow oppression and the dehumanisation of workers in the pursuit of economic growth.
He cited foreign workers being housed in conditions resembling slavery a century ago.
"I cannot accept that," he said.
He said the government was negotiating with source countries individually to reduce recruitment costs, describing agents who held workers' passports as engaging in "modern slavery".
Anwar also said he had negotiated with Myanmar's president on the repatriation of its nationals in Malaysia.
"We have 200,000 Myanmar nationals here, including economic refugees. If they are sent back, human rights groups protest. If they stay here, the people protest," he said.
He said more than 10,000 had since been sent home under the arrangement.
"Anti-foreigner sentiment has sometimes become excessive and is no longer humane," he said.
"Tightening (the policy) will affect certain industries. Loosening it creates serious economic and social problems."
Last month, Anwar said 10,493 Myanmar nationals had been repatriated by air and sea following talks with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing during the latter's official visit to Malaysia.
Myanmar had also agreed to take back between 3,000 and 4,000 of its nationals held at immigration depots, at its own expense.
In November 2024, the government approved a one-off special quota of 24,570 foreign workers for 143 plantation companies to address labour shortages in the sector.
In February 2023, Anwar called for an end to the use of agents in foreign worker recruitment, saying the high costs involved amounted to modern slavery.

49ba3d62b159b1b8: PETALING JAYA: PAS disaran menggunakan pendekatan hujah berfakta bagi menjaga imej parti dan keharmonian masyarakat, berbanding melabel pihak lawan dengan istilah-istilah agama.
Syaza Shukri dari Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia berkata melabel pihak lawan merupakan 'politik murahan', terutama apabila istilah agama digunakan untuk menyerang mereka.

"Rakyat bijak. Kita tahu label-melabel ini 'cheap politics' untuk menakutkan rakyat dan kononnya membabitkan agama dalam isu politik, tetapi hakikatnya hanya perbezaan pendapat atau haluan," katanya kepada FMT.
Mazlan Ali dari Universiti Teknologi Malaysia berkata perbezaan pandangan politik tidak seharusnya menjejaskan hubungan sesama masyarakat dan silaturahim dalam kalangan umat Islam.
Katanya, PAS mempunyai pengaruh yang kuat namun rakyat akan lebih menghormatinya sekiranya ia mengelakkan pendekatan melabel pihak lawan.

"PAS perlu mengkritik kerajaan, kerana tidak ada kerajaan yang sempurna. Sebagai pembangkang, tugas PAS adalah menyemak imbang. Rakyat akan lebih menghormati PAS jika sesuatu kritikan itu berasaskan politik hujah," katanya.
CSA ditandatangani Presiden Bersatu Muhyiddin Yassin dan lima Ahli Parlimen Bersatu lain, serta Ahli Parlimen Muar Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.

CSA memberikan tujuh wakil rakyat itu akses peruntukan pembangunan kawasan Parlimen, yang telah diterima oleh Ahli Parlimen kerajaan sepanjang empat tahun lalu. Ia turut merangka dua reformasi utama yang mesti dilaksanakan Putrajaya sebagai balasan kepada sokongan mereka -- meletakkan had tempoh jawatan perdana menteri dan memisahkan peranan peguam negara dan pendakwa raya sebelum tamat penggal Parlimen.

Kelmarin, media melaporkan Hadi mengumpamakan CSA ditandatangani antara kerajaan dan tujuh Ahli Parlimen pembangkang seperti penipuan dajal – ‘pembohong paling besar’, yang kemunculannya dianggap dalam Islam sebagai antara tanda besar semakin hampirnya Hari Kiamat.
Dalam kenyataan, beliau mendakwa CSA adalah pendekatan dajal pada akhir zaman yang menjadikan kuasa bukan lagi suatu amanah yang wajib ditunaikan kepada semua, tetapi memaksa untuk terus berkuasa.
Beliau berkata, mana-mana parti yang menjadi kerajaan wajib menunaikan amanah kepada rakyat secara langsung tanpa perlu membuat aku janji terlebih dahulu.

Kenyataan Hadi mengundang kritikan pelbagai pihak, antaranya Ketua Pemuda PKR Kamil Munim yang mengingatkan bahawa perjanjian sama pernah ditandatangani sewaktu PAS berada dalam kerajaan, dengan PH pada 13 Sept 2021.
Bekas ahli majlis kerja tertinggi Umno, Puad Zarkashi, pula mempersoalkan sama ada Umno turut dianggap 'dajal kecil', mengingatkan bahawa Umno antara parti yang membentuk kerajaan perpaduan.
Di Dewan Rakyat, Ahli Parlimen Bersatu Suhaimi Abdullah berkata label 'dajal' menimbulkan persoalan mengenai kesungguhan memperjuangkan perpaduan nasional.
Katanya, usaha mencapai persefahaman demi kepentingan rakyat sukar direalisasikan jika Ahli Parlimen yang mengambil pendekatan bekerjasama turut dilabel 'dajal'.
Sementara itu, Ahli Parlimen PAS Ahmad Fadhli Shaari mempertahankan kenyataan Hadi berhubung penggunaan istilah ‘dajal’, yang dikatakan bukan merujuk kepada individu menandatangani CSA.
Katanya, istilah itu merujuk pendekatan dalam CSA yang didakwa meletakkan syarat wakil rakyat perlu memberi sokongan sebelum sesuatu peruntukan disalurkan kepada Ahli Parlimen.
aa48c25e3b808dc7: ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi paid a courtesy call on Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan today.
The meeting, which began at 4pm local time (9pm Malaysian time), lasted about 30 minutes and was held at the Istanbul Congress Centre after the 2026 TRT World Forum opening ceremony.

On bilateral ties, both sides looked forward to strengthening relations following the establishment of the High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council, whose inaugural meeting was held in Ankara in Jan this year.
The discussion also covered raising the bilateral trade target from US$5.6 billion in 2025 to US$10 billion by 2030.
Zahid also congratulated Turkiye on becoming Asean's 12th Dialogue Partner. Malaysia, he said, would work closely with Ankara as country coordinator.
On regional security, Zahid commended Turkiye's role as an interlocutor in Syria, Lebanon and Palestine, including Gaza.

He also praised Ankara's mediation in the Ukraine–Russia war through the "Istanbul Process" and voiced support for its backchannel diplomacy on the United States–Iran conflict, together with Pakistan, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.
Zahid also wished Turkiye success in hosting the 31st meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change summit in Antalya on Nov 11 and 12.
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, is in Turkiye for a four-day working visit from Nov 5 to 8.

7cce833a038d4845: KUALA LUMPUR: The home of former prime minister Najib Razak at No 11 Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, has been declared a prison for the imprisonment or detention of persons in lawful custody.

The declaration was made by home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail under the Prisons Act and published in the Federal Gazette today. The declared area covers all buildings and a land area of 4,559 square metres.
The High Court has issued an Order of Discharge following the settlement of a RM50 million fine imposed on him in the SRC International fund misappropriation case.
The payment is one of the conditions of a conditional royal pardon allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.

However, in a statement this evening, the Attorney-General's Chambers called for a deferral of house arrest and for Najib to be held at Kajang prison pending further scrutiny and clarification of the interpretation of the conditional pardon and the effect of the Order of Discharge.

746f5bb4b0e427ba: SHAH ALAM: Jalan Rawang-Kuala Selangor (B27) at Section 9.90 in Gombak has been closed to all vehicles following a landslide that damaged part of the road structure last night.
The incident was reported about 11pm, involving failures of both the upper and lower slopes, which caused part of the road structure to collapse.
The Selangor Public Works Department (PWD) said the landslide also brought down trees, blocking the entire road.

In a statement, it said the road closure was implemented by the Gombak District PWD, while information on alternative routes was shared through the Facebook pages of PWD Selangor and Gombak this morning.
"The incident is believed to have been caused by heavy rain, which led to a large amount of rainwater infiltrating the ground, increasing soil saturation and pore water pressure on the slopes.
"This caused slope instability and soil movement, resulting in the collapse and damage to part of the road structure," it said.
PWD Selangor said further investigations and technical assessments were under way to determine the actual cause of the incident.
It said a Traffic Management Plan (TMP) had also been activated, including the installation of signs indicating the full road closure and diversion routes to ensure road users' safety.
"Temporary tarpaulin sheets have also been installed on the affected roadside embankment and slope surfaces to prevent erosion and further landslides.
"Debris and fallen trees blocking the road following the upper slope failure are being cleared by the state road concessionaire.
"Continuous monitoring is being carried out by Gombak District PWD and the concessionaire to detect any active movement in the road structure and assess slope stability.

"Construction of a temporary diversion road in the affected area will be carried out to allow light vehicles to pass, subject to technical assessment and safety considerations, including the stability of the slopes," it said.

PWD Selangor said an announcement on the road's reopening would only be made after technical assessments confirmed that the landslide area was safe and the diversion road was suitable for light vehicles.
Road users have been advised to follow all traffic signs and diversion instructions for their safety.

825df45a72b58192: TOKYO: Japan launched a multi-million dollar emergency policy package on Friday to address a sudden wave of hacking incidents.
The country's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has vowed to take action after dozens of businesses reported unauthorised access in recent weeks to their systems and potential leaks of client data.
Hacks and data breaches have ballooned worldwide, with AI's ability to find previously unknown ways to break into computer systems in the global spotlight.

"In light of the current situation involving increasingly serious cyberattacks, all ministers present today have put their heads together to formulate an 'emergency countermeasures package'," Takaichi told her ministers on Friday.

The package would initially be funded by 10 billion yen (US$63 million) available in the government's budget, but the overall cost would likely be higher, with the premier asking her finance minister to figure out how to free up funds for the entire plan.

The package includes security countermeasures partly through the use of AI, strengthening of investigation systems, and reinforcement of support for victims and measures to prevent the spread of damage, she said.
Media reports have said the package includes the creation of a "cyber rescue team" made up of both government and private sector experts.

The government will set up a secretariat within the current fiscal year to coordinate the deployment of the rescue team when support needs are particularly acute, the Yomiuri Shimbun daily, Jiji Press and other reports said.
Takaichi did not mention the cyber rescue team but said that mobilisation was needed to "to keep up with the speed of cyberattacks in the AI era.

"Even at this very moment, incidents of unauthorised access and information leaks are occurring one after another, having a major impact on the lives of our citizens and on corporate activities," she said.
"Let us mobilise the full capabilities of the government to strengthen our nation’s overall capacity to respond," she added.

Chinese artificial intelligence cybersecurity tool Artex was used in several recent hacks of Japanese companies, an information security arm of Japanese IT firm GMO Internet Group Inc said last month.
GMO Internet Group itself is among those that have come under attack.

f7bf69c583dfda3d: The US Department of Justice (DoJ) says its Super Intelligence Task Force (SINTF) is now up and running, after president Donald Trump ordered the move in a memo last month.

Headed up by director of national intelligence Jay Clayton, as well as associate attorney general Stanley Woodward and associate deputy attorney general Stephen Weiss, SINTF's responsibility is to protect the US's lead in artificial intelligence development.

Thursday's announcement, which was littered with the "super intelligence" Trumpism, said the task force will ensure the US's SI/AI leadership remains uncompromised by foreign AI "abuse," including by state and state-backed groups, criminal enterprises, individuals, or corporate entities.

Per Trump's October 13 memo [PDF], SITF will take "affirmative measures, as appropriate," to ensure the US stays ahead in AI development. It did not elaborate on what this nebulous phrase meant, but it can be reasonably assumed this means a breadth of proactive steps.

The memo also stated that the task force will organize the DoJ's criminal and civil lawsuits involving AI, recommend enforcement priorities concerning public safety and AI misuse, develop prosecution guidance for unlawful AI conduct, and feed into legislative proposals to prevent "burdensome regulation."
Addressing a Wall Street Journal tech conference this week, Pentagon CTO and SITF vice chair Emil Michael said the team would release details about its AI regulatory landscape later this month.
The task force will also shoulder various cross-departmental responsibilities, such as "deconflicting investigations, cases, and other matters" among departments and the offices of US attorneys.

According to quotes from senior officials, chief among the concerns facing ordinary US citizens are AI attacks that target individuals, as well as those that aim to disrupt critical infrastructure and other national security interests.
"The creation of the DOJ-SITF marks an important moment for the Department to help advance SI technologies and, at the same time, protect American innovation," said Weiss.

"The Department also has a responsibility to utilize law enforcement tools at our disposal to deter improper use of SI, harden regular reporting on SI risk and response, and ensure companies exercise vigorous internal controls so that SI technology behaves as intended. The Department is committed to protecting all Americans and our business interests."

Trump compelled the US to start using the term "super intelligence" in September, claiming "artificial intelligence," the widely used and original term coined in the mid-1950s, was a better descriptor for the technology's capabilities.
The US government's dedicated website for SI states that "America is in a race for Super Intelligence. We intend to win it."
It also highlights a number of initiatives the government has taken to promote its AI supremacy, including legal guidance to streamline federal approvals, leading to more data centers being built.
The pivot toward renaming the technology in all official capacities raised confusion at the time.

A somewhat contradictory move, the Trump administration heavily promotes its own AI innovators, but in one swoop essentially antiquated the trading name of arguably its most recognizable AI lab, OpenAI.

One financier previously floated the idea that Trump ordered the shift to boost the value of .si domain names, many of which have recently been registered using MAGA-related terms and resold for millions of dollars. There is no categorical evidence that the investments are linked to the Trump family, however. ®
76b9562cffb4e6a4: THAT 213 Malaysians were arrested overseas since 2024 for alleged involvement as drug mules should be a sobering message for the country to take this matter far more seriously.

Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah has told the Dewan Rakyat that drug-trafficking syndicates are targeting young people, including students and graduates, with irresistible financial and material incentives.
These syndicates must know their targets are particularly susceptible to inducements for what may appear to be harmless and routine tasks as human couriers.
Social media also makes it all the more easier for drug traffickers to reach out to potential victims, exploiting their gullibility and naivety.

Malaysians need to understand that ignorance and being unaware of what they carry are unlikely to spare them from prosecution. As is in Malaysia, many other countries have strict drug laws mandating lengthy prison sentences or even the death penalty upon conviction for trafficking.
A seemingly casual favour of carrying a package for someone could cost those implicated their freedom or even their lives.
Parents, universities and educational institutions must be particularly on the lookout and be proactive in educating young people about these syndicates' recruitment practices.

Awareness campaigns should go beyond the usual anti-drug messaging to include practical guidance on being cautious about suspicious job offers, verifying prospective employers and spotting red flags in online recruitment campaigns.

Educating the public on the issue should go hand in hand with enforcement action. The use of social media, e-commerce platforms and messaging applications by syndicates makes it necessary for the police, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, financial institutions and digital platforms to work in concert to identify and disrupt the nefarious recruitment networks.
This message must be drummed home: never accept luggage, parcels or other items from strangers or agree to transport goods overseas without first knowing precisely the contents.
The 213 cases should not be dismissed as isolated incidents or as merely the result of poor judgment.
The syndicates know only too well how trusting and obliging Malaysians can be, which are traits they exploit to the fullest.
A deliberate and increasingly sophisticated recruitment strategy is being employed by these international drug syndicates.
Malaysians must never allow the lure of quick and easy money, free holidays or other enticing perks to cloud their judgment.
The syndicates can be counted on to zero-in on such momentary lapses in judgment in service of their vile intentions.
The price of such mistakes is having to face long legal processes, which could lead to stiff prison sentences, or worse.

"We showed a really quick response and improved a lot last season, and you know it shows what is possible, but again, sustaining it is the key, consistency is the key.

7cd2f6c99f3f33dd: PETALING JAYA: Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) tidak mempunyai kuasa untuk menangguhkan prerogatif pengampunan diraja, dan apa-apa persoalan mengenai perintah mahkamah perlu dibawa ke mahkamah, kata peguam Najib Razak.
Firma guaman Shafee & Co menggesa komisioner penjara menyempurnakan pelepasan anak guam mereka itu untuk menjalani tahanan di rumah tanpa berlengah lagi.
Peguam bekas presiden Umno itu turut berkata, AGC tidak boleh menahan anak guam mereka di Penjara Kajang, menambah bahawa kediaman Najib telah diwartakan hari ini sebagai penjara.

"Memindahkan anak guam kami ke sana tidak mengeluarkan beliau daripada jagaan sah. Ia hanya memindahkan beliau dari satu penjara yang diwartakan ke satu penjara lain yang juga diwartakan," katanya, menambah pemindahan itu selaras dengan titah Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
Katanya lagi, setiap syarat yang ditetapkan oleh Agong telah dipenuhi, 'dan tiada alasan yang sah di sisi undang-undang untuk anak guam kami terus berada di Penjara Karang walau sesaat lagi'.

Terdahulu, AGC berpendapat pelaksanaan tahanan di rumah terhadap bekas presiden Umno itu wajar ditangguhkan buat sementara waktu sehingga penelitian dan penjelasan lanjut berhubung interpretasi perintah pengampunan bersyarat serta kesan ‘order of discharge’ diselesaikan.

AGC berkata, pelaksanaan tahanan di rumah terhadap Najib wajar ditangguhkan buat sementara waktu kerana timbul persoalan perundangan berhubung interpretasi frasa ‘menjalani baki hukuman secara tahanan di rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028 tertakluk sekiranya beliau membayar denda RM50 juta’, dan kesannya terhadap baki hukuman penjara bagi kes SRC International.

Katanya lagi, persoalan mengenai status baki hukuman penjara bagi kes SRC International turut mempunyai implikasi terhadap pelaksanaan hukuman penjara Najib bagi kes 1MDB, khususnya berhubung perintah mahkamah yang menetapkan bahawa hukuman bagi kes 1MDB hendaklah bermula selepas selesai hukuman penjara bagi kes SRC International.

Bagaimanapun, peguam Najib berkata, 'dua interpretasi' yang dibangkitkan oleh AGC berkaitan dengan kesan perintah pengampunan, namun 'AGC tidak berhak enggan melaksanakan terma yang nyata dalam sesuatu pengampunan diraja sementara AGC masih meneliti pendiriannya'.

Peguam Najib berkata, pihaknya melihat kenyataan AGC itu sebagai suatu tindakan mengetepikan titah Agong, mengatakan 'tiada apa-apa dalam kenyataan itu yang boleh menjadi asas untuk terus menahan anak guam kami di Penjara Kajang'.
Katanya lagi, rujukan AGC kepada kes 1MDB 'tidak mengubah apa-apa', dan kes itu tidak mempunyai apa-apa kaitan dengan kewajipan AGC untuk melaksanakan perintah pengampunan dalam kes SRC.
Justeru, peguam Najib menggesa peguam negara supaya menarik balik kenyataan AGC dengan serta-merta.
Sementara itu, peguam Najib berkata, peguam negara ialah anggota lembaga pengampunan dan hadir pada mesyuarat 18 Sept yang mempersembahkan nasihat kepada Agong berhubung perintah pengampunan.

"Sekiranya beliau mempunyai apa-apa kebimbangan tentang terma-terma perintah pengampunan, mesyuarat itulah tempat yang sewajarnya untuk membangkitkannya. Sebaliknya, AGC membangkitkannya buat kali pertama hanya selepas denda dibayar," katanya.
Perkembangan ini menyusuli kenyataan peguam Najib, Farhan Shafee, bahawa Mahkamah Tinggi mengeluarkan perintah tahanan rumah terhadap anak guamnya susulan penyelesaian bayaran denda RM50 juta.
Umno sebelum ini berkata, parti itu telah melunaskan denda yang dikenakan terhadap bekas presidennya itu.

Najib dipenjarakan pada Ogos 2022 selepas Mahkamah Persekutuan mengekalkan sabitan atas kesalahan salah guna kuasa, pecah amanah jenayah dan pengubahan wang haram melibatkan dana SRC International berjumlah RM42 juta.
Dia dijatuhi hukuman penjara 12 tahun dan denda RM210 juta. Pada Januari 2024, pengampunan diraja mengurangkan separuh tempoh hukuman penjaranya dan jumlah denda kepada RM50 juta.

Pada September tahun ini, satu lagi pengampunan bersyarat diberikan kepada Najib, yang membolehkan dia menjalani baki hukuman secara tahanan di rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028, tertakluk sekiranya Najib menyelesaikan pembayaran denda RM50 juta serta pematuhan terhadap syarat-syarat yang ditetapkan.

c16fa94a89f98dcf: UNTAMED chronicles the meteoric rise of Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) from a local football club into one of Asia's most formidable sporting powerhouses.
The 76-minute documentary takes viewers beyond the roar of the stadium and into the inner workings of the club's success.
More than a simple celebration of trophies, the film offers a look into the ambition, discipline, sacrifices and relentless demands that have shaped the Southern Tigers over the past 13 years.

Now streaming on the club's JDT+ platform, 'Untamed' places Regent of Johor and JDT owner Tunku Mahkota Ismail Sultan Ibrahim at the heart of the story, sharing his personal perspective on the vision and decisions behind the club's transformation.

The documentary's strength lies in its access. Viewers are taken inside the dressing room, training ground and management offices — places supporters rarely get to see beyond carefully edited match-day footage.
The inclusion of key figures from management, coaching and playing ranks gives the narrative real depth.

Chief operating officer Alistair Edwards, finance director Datuk Seri Mohamad Jaifuddin Bujang Mohidin, special projects manager Kevin Ramalingam and former sporting director Martin Prest provide insights into the organisation behind JDT's ambitions.

On the pitch, current stars Arif Aiman Mohd Hanapi, Bergson da Silva, Matt Davies and La'Vere Corbin Ong share the spotlight with former captain Safiq Rahim, Safee Sali and former head coach Bojan Hodak.
Their accounts help shift the focus from the final score to the reality of maintaining a winning culture, where expectations remain high even after lifting a trophy.
The documentary proves that JDT's dominance didn't come simply from signing expensive players or assembling a star-studded squad.
Instead, it highlights a philosophy built around solid infrastructure, smart financial planning, professional management, high performance standards and an uncompromising mindset.
With 35 trophies in 13 years — including the historic 2015 AFC Cup triumph that made JDT the first Malaysian club to win the competition — the achievements provide a grand backdrop.
There are lighter moments, too. Candid exchanges and personal anecdotes add genuine personality to what could otherwise have felt like a dry corporate video about sports management.
But 'Untamed' is not without its limits. Compressing over a decade of transformation into just 76 minutes naturally leaves some chapters underexplored.
The controversies, setbacks and tough decisions that came with JDT's rise could have been explored more closely.

The documentary also leans heavily on the club's own voice. While this makes for an engaging showcase of its success, including independent voices and a deeper look at its challenges would have provided a more balanced narrative.
Still, 'Untamed' succeeds in taking the conversation about JDT beyond its trophy cabinet.
It gives real insight into the people, structure and demands behind an institution that has raised expectations for Malaysian football.
For JDT supporters, it is a journey worth looking back on. For neutral fans, it offers a fascinating glimpse into what it takes to build and maintain a winning team.
Ultimately, the documentary's biggest takeaway is that JDT's story is not just about winning silverware, but about the drive to keep raising the bar.
For more details on 'Untamed', visit jdtplus.com.

a8009769f7d8780b: WASHINGTON: Democrats are planning to unleash a flood of new legislation targeting AI systems and data-center development when they take control of the US Congress in January, lawmakers, congressional aides and advocates said.

The plans would mark a sharp shift from the Republican-led Congress, where lawmakers largely focused on promoting AI development and declined to pass legislation restricting aspects of the technology at a time when voters turned against the rapid development of data centres and their extensive power needs.

Democrats plan on introducing bills aimed at shielding consumers from rising electricity costs tied to data centres, requiring independent testing of advanced AI systems and clarifying when AI companies can be held liable for harm caused by their products, they said.
Any legislation would face steep odds while Republican President Donald Trump remains in the White House, as he has repeatedly dismissed calls to write mandatory rules for AI technology.
On Friday, Trump said he would work with US states that "want to become RICH" by embracing AI, without offering details.

But Democratic lawmakers and outside advocates said control of congressional committees would give the party a platform to advance proposals, compel testimony from industry leaders and build support for action if AI systems cause real-world harm. Representative Greg Casar, a Texas Democrat and chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, already said this week that AI executives should be called to testify under oath.

Federal government restrictions on AI development could hurt the industry's profits if they slow the release of new models or prompt the companies to change how their AI tools perform to address concerns that their products are harming people.

Technology shares sold off dramatically on Thursday on growing concerns that a new Congress will slow AI development and also on fears that the massive capital expense on building out AI will not yield sufficient returns.
Stocks on Friday extended their slide in both Europe and Asia following the rout, though Wall Street futures pointed to a modest bounce for the Nasdaq later on Friday.

Senator Chuck Schumer, a New York Democrat who is expected to become majority leader, said on Thursday at an event in Washington that protecting consumers from higher energy costs linked to the rapid expansion of data centers would be among his priorities next year.

Representative Lori Trahan of Massachusetts, one of the Democratic Party's leading voices on AI policy, plans to push legislation requiring independent experts to evaluate leading AI models against safety standards, said Francis Grubar, her deputy chief of staff. Trahan will also pursue legislation clarifying that companies can be held responsible when AI systems act in harmful ways, he said.

Representative Zoe Lofgren, a Democrat from California who is seeking to chair the House Science Committee, said Democrats would focus on developing "responsible regulations for AI while also fostering innovation."

Abdul El-Sayed, a Michigan Democrat who won a Senate seat on Tuesday, called during his campaign for an independent agency to oversee AI regulation with the power to police tech companies developing the technology.

Public concern about AI is already high. Most US voters think Trump's administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to ​write new regulations for the technology, according to a Reuters poll published in October. A crisis could build enough support to overcome presidential opposition to AI regulation, said Ed Mills, who manages policy research at Raymond James.
"The probability of legislation is much higher than people anticipate," he said.

Congress can override a presidential veto with the backing of two-thirds of lawmakers in both chambers. Democrats could also try to insert AI regulation into routine bills that must pass Congress each year, Mills said.

Democrats also plan to use their new authority to intensify scrutiny of the industry's most powerful companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic. Lofgren and other Democratic House committee leaders in October asked OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Alphabet's Google and SpaceX to detail their security practices and report instances of their AI tools taking actions that their designers did not intend.

1c4079f29568663f: Linux Mint 27 is expected next month, and it's starting to take shape. Its flagship desktop, Cinnamon 2.8, is already available.

The team behind the popular, beginner-friendly Linux just released Cinnamon 2.8, which will be the default desktop in Mint 27. Since 2014, Linux Mint versions have been based on the LTS releases of Ubuntu. Since a new LTS, Ubuntu 26.04 "Resolute Raccoon" arrived in late April, that means that a corresponding version of Mint is in development.

The Mint project blog post last month revealed the codename: "Adrien." This is the first male codename since Mint 1.0 "Ada" in 2006, based on the first ever Ubuntu LTS release, 6.06 "Dapper Drake", but the project has run through the whole alphabet since then (except for the letter “Y”.) That blog also revealed it will have a new alarm clock app, but the subsequent Mint Blog post imparted more information.

The Nemo file manager will gain a preview pane, there will be a new and much more capable system resource-monitor program called "Superlight", a new simple manager for compressed archive files (Zip and so on) called "Unfold," and a new, theme-able terminal emulator called "Velocitty." Mint also has a new Community Website, which uses GitHub to manage logins and eliminates the old website's dependency on PHP.

Probably the most significant new feature, though, is that Mint 27 will restore system hibernation. Ubuntu supported hibernation in its early releases, but it has been disabled as standard since 12.04 "Precise Pangolin." Enabling it again is regularly discussed, for instance back in 2020. As we discussed in some detail a year ago, it's a complicated subject and there's a lot that can go wrong.

It seems that Mint's Clément Lefebvre feels he can sort this, and we hope it works out. Support is included in the new version of Cinnamon, among a host of other changes. Its Wayland support is no longer experimental, although the X11 session is still there so users won't be forced to use the new system. The Network Manager applet has better, simpler VPN support and Wi-Fi encryption handling. There are multiple improvements across the desktop: better handling of sound devices, keyboard input layouts, touchpads and gesture support, HiDPI display handling, and better search in the Settings app. The window list control has been upgraded, more things happen in the background for faster desktop starts, and it has better handling and storage of authentication and credentials, including the same Rust-based "oo7" secret store we mentioned in Fedora 45. Screensaver handling is also mentioned – this is particularly problematic under Wayland, as XScreensaver maintainer Jamie Zawinski has covered with some feeling. The Mint blog mentioned this at the start of 2026, when Lefebvre announced the new, slower, annual release schedule.

Cinnamon is not the only desktop environment that has moved to embrace Wayland while also maintaining its support for X.org. Almost exactly two years ago, we reported that the LXQt 2.1 included preliminary Wayland support. That project is very much still in active development, led by Jen-Lee "PCMan" Hong, and version 2.5.0 just appeared, almost simultaneously with Cinnamon 2.8.

Before LXQt, "PCMan" developed the LXDE desktop – which is still around. There's an LXDE spin of Fedora 45, the Raspberry Pi OS uses some of its components, and last year when Debian 13 was released we also noted that its terminal emulator, LXTerminal, had just been updated. This release of LXQt removes its last dependency on an LXDE component – until now, it still used the old menu-cache.

LXQt 2.5 is based on Qt 6.10, and it draws upon some of the components of KDE Plasma. One of these is libkscreen, which manages screens for Plasma. Version 6.8 of this drops X11 support – as does Plasma 6.8 itself – and that broke LXQt's Monitor Settings applet. The team are looking for a workaround and plan to fix this in a minor point release. Aside from this, the desktop's taskbar-style panel has improved sizing support, icon handling, and auto-hide, but most of the improvements in this release are in around its QTerminal terminal emulator.
New LXQt versions usually appear twice a year, around April and November, so this version will likely be in Lubuntu 27.04 in about five months – and available in many other distributions, too. ®
e5fead3728838efb: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has enough rice to last at least six months and fish for eight months should a cyberattack disrupt the country's communication networks, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said the government was prepared to distribute food supplies physically from farms if digital systems were disrupted.
Speaking at the 14th Malaysia Madani Scholars Forum today, Mohamad said the threat of cyber warfare was still at an early stage but was already real.
"The next war will be a cyber war. We must be mentally prepared for this," he said.
He likened the threat to the Star Wars films of the 1970s.
"We saw it as imagination, an illusion. But now it is really starting to happen," he said.
Mohamad asked the audience to imagine going a week without internet or television.
"We can sleep. But how would people order rice? Order fish? Order food supplies?" he said.
He said global power was no longer concentrated in the hands of a single party, with other players now capable of mounting cyber challenges against superpowers.
However, Mohamad assured the public that Malaysia was prepared for such disruptions.
"There is no need to panic, because we have enough rice stock for at least six months. We currently have enough fish for eight months and other food items are also available.
"But if there is a cyberattack and communications are cut, we are prepared through farms to send food supplies physically," he said.
Mohamad stressed that preparations were necessary even if such an attack never materialised.
"But preparation must be there and we must start educating the people to face cyber warfare in the future," he said.
He cited threats by an unnamed party to disrupt global supplies, including through cyber means, if its country came under attack again.
"If this happens, we will face the first Star War in the world," he said.

Mohamad claimed Europe had been harder hit by cyber warfare than countries in this region, citing incidents in which large quantities of vegetables were discarded after disruptions to electricity supplies caused food to spoil.
He also referred to protests involving about a million people in Paris, saying inflation and food security were among their concerns.
"Food and security have become a global agenda. We can have nuclear weapons, we can have modern weapons, but if there is no food, imagine what happens to a country," he said.
"So we must take cyber seriously and we hope it does not happen in Malaysia. That is our hope."

Also on the panel were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, SD Guthrie Bhd president and group chief executive officer Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad, and PNB Research Institute chief executive officer Dr Sarena Che Omar.
Last week, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi reaffirmed that Malaysia had sufficient food supplies to last 6 months.

Media reports have said several countries, including France, the United Kingdom and Japan, had advised households to maintain emergency supplies for at least 3 days amid concerns over conflicts, extreme weather and disruptions to critical services.

81d282f93739d290: PETALING JAYA: The Attorney-General’s Chambers has no powers to delay house arrest for former Umno president Najib Razak, and the AGC must take to court any question it has about the house arrest order, Najib's lawyers said today.

In a statement this evening, the legal firm of Shafee & Co said the commissioner-general of prisons must complete Najib’s release into house arrest without delay, adding that the AGC had no power to hold Najib in Kajang prison in the meantime.

The statement said Najib’s home had been gazetted as a prison, under the authority of the commissioner general of prisons, and that "moving our client there does not take him out of lawful custody, but moves him from one gazetted prison to another", as provided under the conditional royal pardon.
The statement said every condition of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's order for house arrest had been met, "and there is no lawful reason for our client to remain in Kajang prison a moment longer”.
The AGC was urged to withdraw its statement earlier today calling for a deferral of Najib’s house arrest, saying it amounted to disregard for the king's order.

Earlier today, the AGC called for Najib to remain in prison and for his house arrest to be deferred pending a review of the conditional pardon and the Order of Discharge granted by the High Court after payment of a RM50 million fine.

The AGC said complex legal questions had arisen concerning the implementation of the pardon and court order, with implications for Najib’s 15-year prison sentence in a separate 1MDB case, which will commence in 2028.

However, Najib's lawyers said the AGC’s interpretation concerned the effect of the pardon and that it was not "open to the AGC to refuse to carry out the express terms of a royal pardon while it considered its position".

“The attorney-general has no power to stay the royal prerogative of pardon," the statement said, describing the attorney-general’s current stand as amounting to contempt and possibly even treason. "Nothing in it provides any basis for keeping our client in Kajang prison,” it said.
The statement said the AGC's reference to the 1MDB case “changes nothing” and had no bearing on the AGC’s duty to give effect to the pardon in the SRC case.
They questioned why the attorney-general had not raised the legal questions when he attended the pardons board meeting which advised the king on the pardon.

“If he had any concern over its terms, that meeting was the place to raise it. Instead, the AGC raises it for the first time after the fine has been paid,” the legal firm said, adding the AGC had consistently said in public that the only thing standing between Najib and house arrest was payment of the fine.
Umno paid the RM50 million fine today and the High Court issued an Order of Discharge.

a3ed6642a70163d5: WASHINGTON: Employment in the US grew by 165,000 jobs in October, far exceeding analysts' expectations, with the unemployment rate dipping to 4.1%, government data showed on Friday.

The relatively stable labour market has allowed the US Federal Reserve – which has a dual mandate to maintain inflation at a long-term 2% target while ensuring maximum employment – to make fighting stubbornly high prices its priority.
The strong October data could add to pressure for further rate hikes.

That would put the Fed at odds with President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly called for lower borrowing costs and responded to the central bank's rate hike in September by demanding, "LOWER THE INTEREST RATES FOR THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, AND FAST!"
Analysts had expected 65,000 new jobs and the unemployment rate to hold at 4.2%, according to a consensus forecast from Briefing.com.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also revised up job figures for August and September by a combined 84,000 jobs, the department said in a statement.
The revision to September's data showed that the world's largest economy added 60,000 jobs that month, as opposed to 29,000 as previously reported.
"This is a strong report and a real sign of momentum in the labour market," said Ger Doyle, North America regional president at staffing firm ManpowerGroup.

"Demand is clearly picking up in parts of the economy, but we need to see it spread into more industries and create more opportunities for workers before we call this a broader hiring recovery," he added.
The data comes days after midterm elections in which the cost of living weighed heavily on voters.
October's gain was well above the average monthly increase of 48,000 over the prior 12 months, the BLS said.
Professional and business services led the gains, adding 70,000 jobs, far above the sector's average monthly gain of 15,000 over the past year.
Health care added 42,000 jobs, above its average monthly gain of 31,000 over the last year.
The sector has propped up the labour market in the US in the last year, as an ageing population requires more care both in hospitals and at home.
Transportation and warehousing added 25,000 jobs, mostly among couriers and messengers, while manufacturing added 19,000 jobs, the data showed.
Employment in other major sectors, including construction, retail, financial activities and government, was largely unchanged.

Average hourly earnings for all employees were up 3.1% over the past 12 months, the BLS said, with wages continuing to lag behind stubbornly high inflation, meaning most workers are seeing real wage losses.
Raising interest rates tends to cool inflation but can also limit economic activity, which can affect the job market.

1ed52996bc089a42: BRUSSELS: The EU said Friday "a lot of work" was still needed to reach peace in Ukraine and the bloc would decide on its own security matters, after US President Donald Trump touted a deal with Russia involving "all of Europe".

Trump on Thursday predicted a "very big" deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but "all of Europe", in remarks likely to fuel fresh fears on the continent of a pivot towards the Kremlin.
His comments came as Washington floated a broader rewriting of Europe's security architecture as part of an agreement.
"We all wish that we would have a peace deal soon. We are all working in that regard," said EU spokeswoman Paula Pinho.
"But there is a lot of work that needs to go into it, and above all, there needs to be a willingness on the side of the one who first started the war."
Pinho added: "It's obviously up to the EU to decide on matters which affect its security."
Earlier, a Nato spokeswoman said Ukraine's allies are working for a "just and sustainable" end to the war ahead of US-mediated talks next week in Abu Dhabi.

On Thursday, talks in Brussels involving US, Ukrainian, European and Nato officials "built on productive discussions in Miami and Oslo and sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine", she said.

After participating by video link in the talks, Jared Kushner, the president's envoy and son-in-law, wrote that the US was working on "a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace".
Kushner said Washington's "objective is to develop practical arrangements that address the security concerns of all sides".

He insisted that "any arrangements must fully respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independent decision-making of every nation" and said Nato would "remain central to European collective defence".
The US push will likely rattle Washington's European allies, who have long rejected Moscow's desire to rewrite the European security architecture.
Before launching the war in Ukraine in 2022, the Kremlin delivered an ultimatum to Nato which included a demand that the alliance's troops be withdrawn from eastern Europe.
That was rejected by the Western military alliance.

80b0fe9799041a2c: DigiCert has admitted that a botched server migration left an internal system exposed to the internet for more than a year, allowing an unauthorized user to access customer data, including passports, driver's licenses, and other identity documents.
The certificate authority has begun notifying affected customers but has yet to disclose how many people had their information exposed.

In an email seen by The Register, DigiCert confirmed the compromised information included names, business email addresses, phone numbers, and business addresses. Some records may also have contained passports, driver's licenses, utility bills, or other identification documents.

"We are completing a review of identification documents to determine the specific individuals involved," DigiCert told those affected, adding that it would notify those people once the review was complete.

DigiCert's incident report traces the blunder back to February 2025, when an internal business system was moved from a VPN-protected network to a different availability zone. That change also opened the system up to the public internet, where it sat for more than 16 months without DigiCert realizing.

The archive used the same account management platform as DigiCert's customer-facing products, including a self-registration feature that was never supposed to be available on the internal system. This allowed outsiders to create accounts without multifactor authentication and, thanks to a separate permissions flaw, use them to browse archived customer records.

DigiCert found the unauthorized accounts on June 18, 2026, but initially dismissed them as harmless because they weren't assigned to an application. A security researcher raised the alarm about the account creation issue three days later, but it took until July 2 for DigiCert to shut it down.
Unfortunately, someone had already been poking around.

It wasn't until October 12 that DigiCert began investigating whether customer information had actually been accessed. On October 19, it confirmed that an unauthorized account had accessed a subset of archived records between June 27 and July 2.

DigiCert described the affected records as a "small proportion" of its archive but hasn't disclosed how many customers or individuals were caught up in the breach. The company did not respond to The Register’s questions at the time of publication.

DigiCert's postmortem makes for uncomfortable reading. The server move didn't get a proper security review, monitoring failed to pick up suspicious activity, and the access controls weren't much use against self-registered accounts. The company has since switched off self-registration, tightened network access, and added monitoring that might have come in handy a few months earlier.

Certificate authority operations, CertCentral, and DigiCert ONE were unaffected, the company said, adding that customer credentials and issued certificates remain secure. It also found no evidence that the unauthorized account had been used to issue, revoke, or validate certificates.
That’s good news for anyone worried about their certificates, but less so for those who handed DigiCert a copy of their passport. ®

3a8fc5690275a1d0: Millions of hunters will be in fields and wooded areas, where they can help spot and report any signs of screwworm. Michigan Department of Natural ResourcesFor the first time in over 50 years, an infestation of the flesh-eating fly known as the New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax) is spreading on the U.S. mainland, and it is putting livestock and other animals at risk. The New World screwworm doesn’t just attack cattle. All warm-blooded animals are susceptible, including deer and elk, as well as small game and waterfowl. That means hunters headed to the field this fall may be the most important line of defense for spotting this destructive parasite and keeping it from spreading further. As co-directors of the Mississippi State University deer lab, we believe the country’s millions of hunters can serve as a powerful early warning system by keeping a close eye on the state of wildlife they see. Wildlife agencies are already asking them to be vigilant and report any signs of screwworm infestations. The problem with screwworm Unlike other blowflies, New World screwworm larvae feed on living tissue rather than dead tissue. They lay eggs in open wounds or mucosal openings, such as the eyes and nose of livestock, deer or elk. Screwworm larvae are fairly small but destructive. USDA Screwworm larvae later become flies. USDA Wounds as small as tick bites or scratches, as well as natural openings such as the umbilical stump on newborns or on deer’s pedicles, where their antlers grow and are shed, can attract these parasites. Once the eggs hatch, the maggots burrow into the animal’s flesh and feed, enlarging the wound and attracting more flies. Over time, this leads to infection and death. How the US eradicated screwworm in the past All warm-blooded animals are susceptible to the New World screwworm, but America has seen firsthand the harm they can cause to livestock. In the 1950s, livestock producers in the U.S. Southwest lost up to US$100 million annually to New World screwworm infections, equivalent to over $1 billion today. The New World screwworm fly lays its eggs in fresh wounds, where its larvae hatch and eat the flesh. Judy Gallagher/Wikimedia Commons, CC BY The nation was eventually able to eradicate the New World screwworm from the mainland in 1966 using a combination of treating infected animals and raising hundreds of millions of sterilized male flies and releasing them in infested areas. The New World screwworm has a life cycle of only about 21 days, and each female mates only once. Because of that, inundating areas with sterile male flies for a few months, which equates to a few generations of flies, can eradicate a screwworm population. Historical economic impact estimates of New World screwworm cases in the United States before 2025. USDA 2025 Over time, sterile flies were used to push the New World screwworm further south, where they had been contained behind the Darién Gap, Panama’s narrow border region with Colombia. Sterile flies kept the parasite south of Panama for years, but the movement of cattle and wildlife likely brought it north again. Since 2022, the parasites have been reproducing and moving farther northward. There have been hundreds of detections in Mexico and now in the U.S. The Florida Key deer infestation Wildlife have received far less attention than livestock during screwworm infestations, with one exception: In July 2016, the New World screwworm was detected in the Florida Keys in an endangered deer population: the Florida Key deer (Odocoileus virginianus clavium). Signs of a New World screwworm infestation in an animal’s wound. USDA At the time, the Florida Key deer population was estimated at only about 800 to 1,000 individuals. Because they were endangered and isolated, primarily on the islands of Big Pine Key and No Name Key, they were monitored more closely than most wildlife. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service biologists established quarantine zones. They inspected more than 16,900 animals – dogs, cats, a pig and a raccoon were also found with larvae – and they released 150 million sterile flies across the area. The islands lost 9% to 20% of the total Key Deer population, but the New World screwworm was declared eradicated there on March 23, 2017, less than a year after it was discovered. Screwworm is back In June 2026, screwworm was back in the United States. A rancher discovered the first New World screwworm case in a calf near La Pryor, Texas. A few more cases were confirmed in livestock and domestic animals in Texas and New Mexico. The number of cases had reached 116 detections in animals as of Nov. 5, 2026, including in two elk shot by hunters in Texas. The U.S. government has started ramping up production of sterile flies to try to keep the parasites from spreading. The state of Texas encouraged ranchers and others to report any signs of screwworm after the first cases appeared there in 2026. Joel Angel Juarez/Getty Images Although there have been only a couple of cases reported in wildlife, that isn’t necessarily reassuring. Wildlife are far more likely to carry the parasite without being detected. Once the screwworm is detected, treatment would also be much more complicated for wildlife than for livestock, because wildlife cannot be treated individually and thus are more dependent on the use of sterile flies to eradicate screwworm. For this reason, quickly identifying areas with New World screwworm and targeting those areas by releasing sterile flies would be more important than ever. Tapping an army of conservationists: Hunters Fortunately, there is an army of conservationists across the country who spend much of their time afield. These conservationists are also known as hunters. According to the latest U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service National Survey of Fishing, Hunting, and Wildlife-Associated Recreation, nearly 11.5 million hunters pursue big game and spend part of the fall and winter in the field hunting ungulate species such as deer and elk. Hunters can be the first line of defense in tracking screwworm infections in wildlife. Lovz2hike via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA White-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) hunters alone are expected to harvest about 6 million deer during the 2026-27 season and will observe millions more. Hunters also review tens of millions of wildlife pictures collected each year by game cameras used for scouting. That level of surveillance can’t be matched. New Mexico’s Department of Agriculture has already called on hunters to report any suspicious larvae, particularly in Grant and Otero counties, where screwworm has been found in livestock. Hunters of all kinds, everywhere, can help. What to watch for as a hunter If you’re a hunter, be on the lookout for wounded animals, especially those with visible maggots, and for unusual behaviors such as restlessness, lethargy, or biting or licking wounds. Do not move harvested animals from the field if they show signs of a New World screwworm infection. Doing so could further spread the parasite. Instead, contact the area’s state wildlife agency, the U.S. Department of Agriculture office or a local veterinarian immediately. As hunting seasons get underway across the country, an army of conservationists will be in the field, and they have an important role to play in detecting and managing screwworm’s spread. Hunters already contribute to conservation through license fees, excise taxes and keeping wildlife populations at healthy densities. In the face of New World screwworm, their observations may be most valuable for protecting livestock. 677d069e14533321: SHAH ALAM: Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri (exco) Selangor memutuskan semua kerja pembangunan di Puncak Alam dihentikan segera sementara pelan migitasi banjir serta Penilaian Impak Alam Sekitar dinilai semula.

Menteri Besar Amirudin Shari berkata, pada masa yang sama, Jalan Batu Arang di Rawang akan ditutup sementara oleh Jabatan Kerja Raya (JKR) susulan runtuhan tebing serta memberi ruang untuk kerja-kerja pembaikan dijalankan.

“Tambahan kepada itu, kerja mitigasi banjir baik yang berskala kecil ataupun besar di seluruh negeri terutamanya kawasan yang berisiko lebih tinggi perlu dipercepatkan dengan kadar amat segera dan bukan mengikut jadual konvensional memandangkan hujan dijangka hampir setiap hari.

“Kita sedang menghadapi krisis perubahan iklim dan budaya kerja mitigasi banjir perlu sepadan dengan cabaran yang sedang dihadapi agar sebarang kemudaratan kepada rakyat dapat dielakkan,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Amirudin berkata, kerajaan negeri menyedari kejadian hujan yang mengakibatkan insiden banjir di beberapa kawasan telah menyusahkan rakyat, terutamanya mereka yang pergi dan pulang dari tempat kerja serta mengambil anak dari sekolah, sehingga membawa keresahan apabila hujan.

Justeru, katanya, setiap teguran yang dizahirkan rakyat terhadap agensi kerajaan mesti diterima secara terbuka dengan komitmen untuk melipatgandakan usaha membantu mangsa yang telah terkesan dengan banjir serta usaha mengelakkan banjir daripada terus berulang setiap hari.
